This argument really needs to have the plug pulled. Look, it's pretty simple:

You can either have free speech, or you can have rules. You can't have both. If Voat is really the bastion of free speech everyone keeps trying to make it out to be, then you cannot be shackled with "content rules". That is the problem with reddit, there are people that curate the content. If that is what you want, then fine, go back there.

Now having said all that, I don't think OP is calling for content curation, although there are some on this site that think it is a good idea which is absolutely amazing to me. How anyone could not see that content curation is the reason reddit is censorship is beyond me... but I digress....

OP is simply asking that you think about where you post. There is nothing wrong with civil, voluntary discourse as long as nobody is silenced, and no posts are removed for "organization".

It's possible to have curation and free speech on the same site; it's having them in the same sub that's the issue. It also seems pretty damn obvious to me that removing off topic content is not the same thing as censorship (as so much of the voat community claims. I've seen political stuff in /v/gaming, that are not, by any stretch of the imagination, related to games, where, if ChillyHellion removes it, he gets hate from the poster.), people go to certain communities for certain realms of content, and removing irrelevant content is simply a part of maintaining that dedicated space (especially since we have the modlog). The system subs, and any personal subs one creates, and /v/whatever are ALL free speech platforms, AND get more traffic than anywhere else on the site. Ideally, those locations should be moderated in a janitorial only manner (and, in my experience, they have been). If people want curation, why should you stop them? If they want free speech, not only is there plenty to go 'round, but they can and will create a new sub with that in mind.

All's I'm trying to say is when voat keeps getting touted as this "censorship-free" site, it should be noted that is not in fact true. There is censorship here, just like on reddit, and for exactly the same reason: As long as there is an irrational human curating the content, you will have censorship.

Now, if you're fine with that, fine... you seem to be on the side of preferring a little censorship so you don't have to look at "shitposts".
